line: Happiness, the best the waters can give: nine cups full and overflowing, feeling brought to its height in delight and good fortune. It is luck as much as merit, the wish come true, the banquet laid. Drawn, the card promises contentment and fulfilment, with the quiet reminder that no satisfaction is a final rest and that fullness is the soil of the next change. Jupiter, the planet of fortune, blesses the placid waters of Pisces here, in Yesod, the Foundation.

quotes.quote: The Nine of Cups is called Happiness. This is a peculiarly good card, because happiness, as the word implies, is so much a matter of luck: the card is ruled by Jupiter, and Jupiter is Fortune.
In this card is the pageant of the culmination and perfection of the original force of Water.

But the consonance of Laetitia with this card amounts to little less than an identity; the wine is poured by Ganymede himself, unstinted vintage of true nectar of the Gods, brimful and running over, an ordered banquet of delight, True Wisdom self‐fulfilled in Perfect Happiness.
In the symbol are nine cups perfectly arranged in a square; all are filled and overflowing with Water.
These cards are attributed to Yesod. After the double excursion into misfortune, the current returns to the middle pillar. This Sephira is the seat of the great crystallization of Energy.
Jupiter in Pisces is indeed good fortune, but only in the sense of complete satiety. The fullest satisfaction is merely the matrix of a further putrefaction; there is no such thing as absolute rest.
